newsitem.title: USA: Biodynamics says needs capital infusion.
newsitem.headline: Biodynamics says needs capital infusion.

text.p: Biodynamics International Inc said Tuesday that it is talking with its major creditors in the hopes of reaching a refinancing agreement that would inject at least $1 million dollars in working capital into its coffers and carry it through the September quarter.

The company said that at a July 31 board meeting, members determined that the recent bans imposed by Japan and Italy on certain processed tissue will have a materially adverse effect on the company which could result in a curtailment of operations before the end of August.

Biodynamics told Reuters it is hoping for a finalized refinancing program before the end of the month and in its statement said any additional capital and conversion of debt to equity is likely to result in a significant dilution of value for existing shareholders. But it said there could be no assurance that funding would come on a timely basis.
No layoffs of the 80 employees in Germany and the roughly 10 to 15 employees in the U.S. are planned as of today, but that decision depends upon any new financing agreement, the company told Reuters.

The maker of bioimplants for tissue repair said in March the Japanese Ministry of Health banned all uses of human dura mater, including Biodynamics' Tutoplast dura matter product, upon the recommendation of the World Health Organization (WHO).
In May, the company said, the Italian government imposed a moratorium on the shipments of human dura mater, pending an investigation by European health authorities.

The company said it planned to lodge a protest with the WHO and request a reinstatment of its product from the Japanese authorities at the time. It also said it would appeal to European health authorities that its product is safe.
